officialTitle: Durvalumab with first-line chemotherapy in previously untreated malignant pleural mesothelioma (DREAM): a multicentre, single-arm, phase 2 trial with a safety run-in

design.sampleSizeSourceQuote: Between Dec 28, 2016, and Sept 27, 2017, 55 participants were enrolled.
design.notes: Single-arm phase 2 trial with safety run-in, nine hospitals in Australia; all histological subtypes eligible. Non-comparative evidence; led to the randomised phase 3 DREAM3R trial (protocol only identified in PubMed).

clinicalQuestion: Is durvalumab given with and after first-line cisplatin-pemetrexed active and safe in advanced pleural mesothelioma?

pico.population: Previously untreated pleural mesothelioma unsuitable for surgery, ECOG PS 0-1
pico.intervention: Durvalumab with cisplatin-pemetrexed for up to six cycles, then durvalumab for up to 12 months

arms.label: Durvalumab + cisplatin-pemetrexed
arms.regimen: Durvalumab + cisplatin (or carboplatin) + pemetrexed, then durvalumab
arms.dosing: Cisplatin 75 mg/m2, pemetrexed 500 mg/m2 and durvalumab 1125 mg IV day 1 every 3 weeks for up to six cycles; carboplatin AUC 5 permitted; durvalumab continued up to 12 months
arms.doseSourceQuote: All participants received cisplatin 75 mg/m, pemetrexed 500 mg/m, and durvalumab 1125 mg intravenously on day 1 of a 3-weekly schedule for a maximum of six cycles. Change from cisplatin to carboplatin with an area under the curve of 5 was permitted. Durvalumab was continued for a maximum of 12 months.

publications.title: Durvalumab with first-line chemotherapy in previously untreated malignant pleural mesothelioma (DREAM): a multicentre, single-arm, phase 2 trial with a safety run-in.
publications.label: Primary analysis

outcomes.sourceQuote: 54 patients were eligible and were followed up for a median of 28·2 months (IQR 26·5-30·2). 31 (57%; 95% CI 44-70) of 54 patients were alive and progression-free at 6 months.

safety.sourceQuote: The most common grade 3-4 adverse events were neutropenia (seven [13%] patients), nausea (six [11%]), and anaemia (four [7%]).

A total of 60 serious adverse events occurred in 29 participants, five of which were considered possibly related to durvalumab. Five patients died during the study treatment; none of these five deaths were attributed to study treatment.

strengths: Prospective multicentre trial with safety run-in
limitations: Single-arm phase II evidence; no comparator
Primary endpoint (6-month PFS) is a surrogate

clinicalImplications.text: Single-arm phase II data showing promising activity and acceptable safety of durvalumab with cisplatin-pemetrexed, justifying randomised phase 3 evaluation; not practice-changing on its own.

tumourBoardPearl.text: Hypothesis-generating single-arm evidence: confirmation requires the randomised phase 3 DREAM3R results.

curation.notes: All numbers transcribed from the PubMed abstract of PMID 32888453. Registry is the Australia New Zealand Clinical Trials Registry as printed. DREAM3R: only the protocol (PMID 35078853) was found in PubMed; no results ingested.
